title: Vertex Enumeration for Sharp ATE Bounds with Multi-Valued Instruments and No Monotonicity
banked_reason: User-directed stop: the contribution was misframed at field tier; Boushehrian et al. already prove a broad multivalued-IV lower bound, and this run's quantitative strengthening is incremental rather than field-novel.
gap_reasons: User novelty judgment: BBAK already proves a broad lower bound for the multivalued-IV vertex family; this run improves that lower bound quantitatively but does not establish a sufficiently distinct field-level contribution.

The originally advertised polynomial-delay sound-and-complete enumerator was not completed; the surviving results are recognition, parent-map, complexity partials, and stronger non-exhaustive vertex-count lower bounds.
The run was stopped during a D0 source-faithfulness repair before the final D0.5 derivation-tier verdict and before any F-stage formalization.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved substantial partial structure: polynomial-time exact-signature recognition, a global parent-map framework, universal strict incompleteness of the literal BBAK family, and strengthened finite lower bounds including the (2,3) 27-vertex/21-omission certificate and its n=2 all-l lifting. The central unconditional deterministic polynomial-delay child/enumeration theorem remained open, and the user judged the surviving lower-bound improvement incremental relative to BBAK's existing broad lower bound. The run was hard-stopped during D0 round 20 and never entered formalization.
tldr:
In the finite response-type IV model with binary treatment, ordered \(n\)-point outcomes, \(l\) instrument arms, and no monotonicity, the gauge-fixed upper-dual section removes the \((l-1)\)-dimensional lineality and indexes the sharp ATE endpoint by M-distinct vertices. Exact activity signatures are recognizable in polynomial time, and the published arm-indexed family is strictly incomplete for every \(n\ge2\) and \(l\ge3\). For binary outcomes, the strongest uniform certificate is
\[|\mathcal V_{2,l}|\ge6\binom l2+9\binom l3=\frac32l^2(l-1),\qquad |\mathcal V_{2,l}\setminus\mathcal F^{\mathrm{BBAK}}_{2,l}|\ge\frac{l(l-1)(3l-2)}2.\]
Its \(l=3\) specialization gives the certified lower bounds \(27\) and \(21\). These are lower bounds, not exact multi-arm counts. The sharp endpoints are finite minima and maxima of observable linear functionals, while unconditional deterministic polynomial-delay enumeration for arbitrary \((n,l)\) remains open.
gap: For multi-valued instruments, existing compatibility characterizations and analytical comparator constructions do not provide a complete list of M-distinct quotient-dual vertices. Generic inequality-based vertex enumeration expands a response-type system with \(2^l n^2\) inequalities. The unresolved algorithmic gap is specifically unconditional deterministic inverse-child generation with polynomial delay and polynomial-time exhaustion at degenerate vertices; it is not compatibility characterization or numerical linear-program identification.
fill:
The contribution supplies actionable finite linear-functional representations of the sharp ATE endpoints indexed by \(\mathcal V_{n,l}\), proves that the literal Boushehrian--Badri--Akbari--Kiyavash family is strictly incomplete for all \(n\ge2\) and \(l\ge3\), retains the universal additive deficit theorem, and establishes
\[|\mathcal V_{2,l}|\ge\frac32l^2(l-1),\qquad |\mathcal V_{2,l}\setminus\mathcal F^{\mathrm{BBAK}}_{2,l}|\ge\frac{l(l-1)(3l-2)}2.\]
It also isolates the sole enumeration residual: converting polynomial-time parent evaluation and candidate-ray verification into an unconditional deterministic child iterator for nonsimple vertices.
